boredom_findings.where: default draw (the core loop, i.e. the shell-prompt/MOTD use case)
boredom_findings.what_gets_stale: No anti-repeat memory. First 12 draws produced the same Conway quote twice IN A ROW (draws 7 and 8) and 'All programmers are optimists' twice within 9 draws. Arithmetic: with uniform draws from 50, P(at least one repeat in 7 daily draws) = 1 - (0.98*0.96*0.94*0.92*0.90*0.88) ~= 35.6%. Measured: 30 scripted draws yielded 23 distinct quotes.
boredom_findings.suggestion: A tiny recency guard (stash last N indices, or reroll once on collision with the previous pick), or promote the README's --seed $(date +%j) recipe into a first-class --daily flag.

boredom_findings.where: the corpus itself (read via --list, felt across 12 manual draws)
boredom_findings.what_gets_stale: The curation is 100% greatest-hits; every draw is a line a working developer can finish from its first three words. No deep cuts. Concentration: Dijkstra is 7 of 50 entries = 14% of all draws.
boredom_findings.suggestion: Keep the canon but salt it: roughly a third familiar anchors, two-thirds lines the reader has plausibly never seen.

boredom_findings.where: TTY presentation of the attribution line
boredom_findings.what_gets_stale: The stated aesthetic says 'attribution is dim, not loud; the aphorism is the product', but the attribution renders at full weight identical to the quote. There is no TTY styling path at all. The four-space indent does some of the work, but the eye lands on the author name as hard as the quote. Not what wears out with use — it never delivers the promised quiet hierarchy.
boredom_findings.suggestion: Emit dim styling around the attribution only when stdout isTTY (keeping pipes byte-clean, which they already are).

boredom_findings.what_gets_stale: Typo'd or guessed tags get the generic 'aphorism: no aphorism matches those filters' with no hint that the tag simply doesn't exist, and --help's remedy is a node|jq|sort pipeline. A CLI that can enumerate its own tags shouldn't outsource that to jq.
boredom_findings.suggestion: Add --tags (print the vocabulary), and/or name the valid tags on stderr when the failed filter was a tag.
